rv.q: Her sardonic, cavorting, firecracker performance doesn’t quite conceal the weakness in her writing and the nagging sense of improbability.
Reilly’s strong writing shines through the performance’s chaos and ferocity, conjuring suspense, purpose, and high stakes.

Although the show is clear, entertaining and politically illustrative of the dead hand of the profit system, it does so in a predictable, light way that never really explores the various plot elements...

Reilly has a point to make about how authentic female sexual agency can end up being commoditised and monetised by men, and the toll that sex work, of one kind or another, sometimes takes on those involved.
Just like its protagonist, the show fails to hold on to its own identity.
The result is a show well worth paying attention to - after all, if attention really is currency, ROLEPLAY is full of riches.
Roleplay is a frustrating mix of a hugely charismatic performance with a script that doesn’t quite do justice to its subject matter.
Plain and purposeless, this play about a problematic podcaster isn’t worth watching or listening to.

cn.t: Reilly's energetic performance in this podcast-satire earns laughs, but critics find the writing thin and the Edinburgh Fringe hit loses some sparkle in its London transfer, leaving audiences entertained yet ultimately empty.
